cond_0610.intro: We are looking for a Legal Research Analyst I to join our team. The role provides legal and business research and reference assistance to attorneys and staff, and reports to the Director, Research.
cond_0610.responsibilities:
Provide reference, research, and support to Legal Research Analysts, Attorneys, and Staff in a timely and efficient manner. Where applicable, provide in-depth analysis and summarization of results. Bill time to client/matters as appropriate.
Provide consultative research and reference support, advising lawyers on the optimal strategy and source selection to obtain the most authoritative and cost-effective results.
Conduct in-depth legal, corporate, financial, and/or general research for lawyers, staff, and clients by using the appropriate mix of the firm's external and internal legal, business, and news resources.
Coordinate with other members of the Practice Innovation & Legal Solutions Department on projects, and with the firm's other departments and teams, as required.
Assist in the dissemination and organization of information obtained from print and electronic resources and databases.
Document and package research findings clearly and concisely.
Monitor news, legislative, and regulatory developments as required.
Deliver research training to attorneys and staff and assist in the development of new research and reference offerings.
Stay current on research resources, technologies, and search techniques. Keep department leadership informed of potential additions and/or enhancements to research services.
Participate in team initiatives to promote research resources, tools, and services.
Work beyond scheduled hours as required.
Handle additional related projects as assigned.

Expert-level knowledge of English language skills, including punctuation, spelling, grammar, and writing skills.
Advanced proficiency in Lexis, Westlaw, and a wide range of other standard and specialized legal and business research platforms.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office applications such as Microsoft Outlook, Excel, and Word, Adobe Acrobat, and other common legal systems; the ability to quickly learn and apply new technologies and workflows; and the ability to type 60 WPM.
Strong written communication and clear, direct verbal reporting skills, with a commitment to providing quality work product and sound customer service; knowledge of office practices and procedures, including telephone etiquette.
Ability to work independently and carry projects through to completion, as well as contribute to a service-oriented team.
Highly developed organizational skills.
Fundamental knowledge of legal and business research resources used by global law firms.
Proficiency in online research and legal databases.
Knowledge of database structure and theory.
At least 2 years of experience providing reference and research, preferably in a law or business library.
Advanced degree (MLS, MLIS) in library science, library information science, or a related field (required); or currently enrolled in an advanced degree program (required).
